question.edited: How is power delivered to the 24 Volt net?

answer.edited:
`@ PLG1:B +` Terminal `PLG1:B "PLG1B" +` of the 30 Amp electrical plug brings 115 Volts AC to net `L1 "L1" +`. `~`  

So now we have power on terminal `DISC1:L1 "DISC1L1" +` of the electrical disconnect. `~`  

When this disconnect is switched to the on position `@ CB1:1 +`, power goes to the 8 Amp circuit breaker, `CB1 +`. `~`  

When CB1 is switched to the on position `@ PS1:L1 +` the DC power supply `PS1 +` becomes energized and it converts AC power to 24 Volts DC. `~`  

`PS1:+ +` is the power supply's output terminal. `~`  

`@ CB2:1 +` The 20 Amp circuit breaker `CB2 +` receives the 24 Volt output from the power supply. `~`  

When this circuit breaker is closed `@ CB2:2 +` power goes to `@ TB-24E1-A:1` the main 24 Volt terminal block. `~`  

Now the 24 Volt DC distribution `24E-1 +` becomes energized. `~`  

`PS1:-1 "PS1 negative 1"` the power supply's minus terminal runs to terminal `TB-0V:3 "TB0V3"` at the neutral terminal block and establishes the zero Volt net `0V ""`. `~`  

`PS1:-2`, the power supply's second minus terminal, bonds the neutral zero volt net to the chassis ground at terminal `TB-GND-B:2`. `~`  

The system is now energized and ready to run `@ 24E-1 +` `@ 0V +`.
